note: Mock macro risk-intelligence feed + project policy notes for TradeShield's RAG retriever (AI-11). Calibrated to the June 2026 Strait of Hormuz war-premium narrative. Not real intelligence; demo data only.

documents.text: Escalating US-Iran conflict and the threatened closure of the Strait of Hormuz are the dominant driver of a broad commodity war premium across both energy and metals. Cargoes transiting or loading near the Gulf carry elevated war-risk surcharges; cargoes loading ex-Singapore avoid the transit war exposure but not the benchmark price risk.

LME copper is near record highs (~USD 13,700/MT) on Chilean supply weakness and US tariff arbitrage. Realized volatility is elevated, so RWA collateral valuation against copper cargo should apply a war-premium haircut before pricing the discount.

Brent is near USD 95/bbl, up ~43% year-on-year, with falling US inventories. Large daily swings mean crude-backed RWA collateral needs a volatility haircut on the embedded war premium; the benchmark, not the route, is the main price risk for ex-Singapore loadings.

Marine war & strikes clauses are repricing sharply; underwriters are shortening cover windows and adding Gulf exclusions. Verify that ICC(A) all-risks plus war cover remains valid through the full transit, with a buffer beyond ETA, or the cargo may be under-insured at delivery.
Yangshan discharge berth waiting times are slightly above seasonal norms but within normal range; no material delay risk currently priced for copper-cathode discharge at Shanghai.

Energy-driven inflation is pressuring the Korean won. Because the buyer pays in USD under the L/C, direct FX exposure to the financing pool is limited; KRW weakness is a buyer-side, not pool-side, risk.
Counterparty and vessel screening against sanctions lists shows no hits for the demo trade parties; sanction risk is low but must be re-screened if the route or counterparties change.

1 RWA = 1.00 USD is a TARGET redemption value, not a guaranteed repayment. Investor returns come from buying at a discount and from trade repayment; actual redemption depends on importer payment, cargo settlement and insurance coverage. Demo uses permissioned mock investors and does no real fundraising.

Target redemption exposure must stay within AI-verified collateral times the redemption coverage limit (default 0.9). This collateral guardrail caps how much can be issued and acts as a floor on the issue price.

The RWA discount is priced as a share of the exporter's verified trade profit: faster payout gives up a larger share (FAST 50% / BALANCED 33% / LOW_COST 20% base), risk adds to the share, and the issue price is cash/(cash + share x profit).
